expectations.text: Module has a docstring with a one-line summary of what the module provides
expectations.evidence: First line: "Token-bucket rate limiter with blocking and non-blocking acquisition."

expectations.text: TokenBucket class docstring includes an Attributes: section documenting public attributes
expectations.evidence: Class docstring (lines 18-23) has only summary prose; no Attributes: section anywhere. Public attributes are documented as @property docstrings instead, which does not satisfy the assertion.

expectations.text: acquire and try_acquire have docstrings with Args: and Returns: sections; Raises: present where the code raises for invalid input
expectations.evidence: Both methods have Args:, Returns:, and Raises: ("ValueError: If n is not positive or exceeds capacity."), matching the ValueError raised via _check_amount.

expectations.text: All docstrings use triple double quotes with descriptive (not imperative) first lines ending in a period
expectations.evidence: All 9 docstrings use """; first lines are descriptive third-person ending in periods, e.g. "Initializes a full bucket.", "Attempts to take `n` tokens without blocking.", "Credits tokens accrued since the last refill."

expectations.text: With type annotations present, docstrings describe semantics without repeating the types
expectations.evidence: Args entries give semantics only, e.g. "rate: Token refill rate in tokens per second; must be positive." — no "(float)" or type restatement.

expectations.text: try_acquire's Returns: explains the True/False semantics; acquire documents its blocking behavior
expectations.evidence: try_acquire Returns: "True if the tokens were taken, False if too few are available."; acquire summary: "Takes `n` tokens, blocking until they are available."

expectations.text: Any inline comments are separated from code by at least two spaces and explain intent rather than restating code
expectations.evidence: No trailing inline comments in code; the only comment (lines 113-114) is an own-line block comment explaining intent: "so waiters neither spin nor oversleep".

expectations.text: Thread-safety behavior is stated in the class or module docstring (either safe or not — just stated)
expectations.evidence: Class docstring first line: "A thread-safe token-bucket rate limiter."

expectations.text: Free prose of every docstring (summary plus expanded description, excluding structured sections) is at most 3 sentences
expectations.evidence: Counts: module 1 sentence (+example lead-in fragment); class 2; __init__ 1; rate 1; capacity 1; _refill 2; _check_amount 1; try_acquire 1; acquire 1 — all within 3.

expectations.text: No usage-example blocks in the module or class docstrings
expectations.evidence: Module docstring lines 3-8 contain "Typical usage example:" with a code block (bucket = TokenBucket(...); bucket.acquire(); ...).

expectations.text: Each Args:/Returns:/Raises:/Attributes: entry is a single short sentence
expectations.evidence: Every entry is one sentence, e.g. "n: Number of tokens to take; must be positive and at most capacity." and "True once the tokens are taken, False if the timeout expired first."

summary.notes: Concise, well-formed Google-style docstrings, but the class docstring omits the required Attributes: section and the module docstring includes a usage-example block forbidden by the CC1 tier.
